difficulty_reason: The lemma characterizes conservative families of points by a condition on sections: for any two distinct sections of a sheaf over an object there is a point and an element of the value of the corresponding functor separating them (statement lines 9309-9318). The proof is a complete argument in both directions: two distinct sections give distinct maps from the representable sheaf, which the companion detection result separates at some point, and the identification of the stalk of the representable sheaf yields the required element (proof lines 9321-9332); conversely, for a map which is an isomorphism on all stalks injectivity is immediate and surjectivity is reduced to the injectivity of the codiagonal, which holds on all stalks by hypothesis (proof lines 9334-9346). The non-formal content is the unwinding of the two formulations. The claim is H2: both directions written out with each input named.
